title: Causal change safety harmonizer: batching-aware mitigation and state reconciliation
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Recent config changes to batching and cache TTLs have produced intermittent cost spikes and transient inference errors. Existing safeguards (simple thresholds + canary) are brittle for workload-dependent regressions where batching distribution shifts or KV cache state desynchronizes across nodes. This ticket implements a causal-change safety harmonizer that: (1) ties telemetry signals to specific config deltas using causal attribution, (2) applies batching/caching mitigation recommendations automatically or semi-automatically, and (3) performs safe state reconciliation across runtime shards to avoid noisy rollbacks.
goal: Reduce cost-regression incidents caused by configuration changes by 50% and eliminate KV-cache desync-induced errors for staged applies, while enabling automated safe mitigations for clear causal signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For simulated config changes in staging, the system must detect causal link between change and perf/cost regression within 10 minutes 90% of the time.
2) Automated mitigation (throttle batching window / revert cache TTL / enable prefix-caching) can be triggered and rolled forward or paused by policy without human intervention for low-risk changes.
3) Safe state harmonizer can reconcile KV cache state across 95% of shards after a config flip without requiring full restart or full cache invalidation.
4) New telemetry panels (cost-per-token by model+batch-size, KV-cache-hit delta by shard) are live in Grafana and have alert rules with SLO guardrails configured.
5) Playbook for manual escalation and a one-click mitigation in the Console are available and tested by SRE runbook drill.
6) End-to-end canary -> staged-rollout -> mitigation flow exercised in a canary run without customer-visible errors.
additional: No production incident regressions attributable to batching/caching applies in a 2-week window post-rollout
proposed_solution: Design: 1) Attribution layer: augment config-apply pipeline to include a lightweight causal context token attached to traces and metrics (config-change-id). When a telemetry anomaly emerges, use temporal cross-correlation + change-id attribution to produce a likelihood score that the change caused the anomaly. 2) Mitigation rule engine: rule set expresses low/medium/high-risk actions (e.g., reduce max-batch-size by 20%, lower cache-ttl, enable aggressive prefix caching, or route traffic to fallbacks). Rules include preconditions (confidence threshold, customer-impact budget) and postconditions (verify metric recovery). 3) State harmonizer: a reconciliation component that can (a) perform targeted cache invalidation on specified prefixes across shards, (b) stream lightweight state diffs and resync KV entries for nodes that missed warmed prefixes, and (c) optionally shadow-apply the config to a subset of nodes to prepopulate KV before ramp. 4) Safety UI + Ops: Console integration to visualize change-id, confidence score, recommended mitigation, one-click apply and rollback (with audit trail). 5) Testing harness: deterministic workloads in staging to validate heuristics and run regression sims for batching distribution shifts.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing telemetry pipeline (metrics + traces) and add change-id tag to spans and metric labels.
- Lightweight causal model: start with Granger-ish temporal correlation + feature enrichment (batch-size distribution, prefix-hit-rate delta, request p95). Move to Bayesian scoring if necessary.
- Mitigation actions must be idempotent and safe: we will introduce 'mitigation transactions' that can be applied and reversed.
- Harmonizer resync will operate via gRPC to runtime nodes and use incremental snapshot IDs to avoid full cache flush.
- Security: ensure change-id propagation does not leak secrets; small security review required for gRPC endpoints.
- Performance: reconciliation operations must be rate-limited and scheduled during low-util windows where possible.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime-safety feature flag. 2) Internal canary: enable for staging and two internal customers (low-traffic). 3) Observe for 72 hours, tune thresholds. 4) Incrementally enable for 10% / 30% / 100% of tenants with automated rollback policy if confidence-based mitigation fails health checks. 5) After 1 week stable, open to broader rollout. Manual stopgap: Console 'pause mitigations' toggle and the ability to demote automated actions to 'suggest only'.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- New Grafana dashboards: 'Config-change causal heatmap', 'Batching distribution by model', 'KV-resync success rate'
- Alert rule: if confidence_score>0.8 && cost-per-token increases >20% for 15m -> trigger mitigation-as-suggestion (P1) and open incident.
- Alert rule: if harmonizer reconciliation fails >5% of shards during apply -> escalate to SRE on-call.
- Telemetry SLA: causal_attribution latency < 10m in 95th percentile.
risks_and_mitigation: Risks: false-positive mitigations could cause unnecessary throttles; heavy reconciliation may increase runtime load; change-id tagging may bloat metrics cardinality. Mitigations: conservative initial thresholds, backoff/rate-limit reconciliation, use sampling for high-cardinality tags, and opt-in for aggressive harmonization behaviors.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for rule engine and mitigation transactions.
- End-to-end sim harness that replays historical workloads and injects synthetic config deltas to validate attribution.
- Chaos test: random shard drop during resync to ensure harmonizer handles partial failures.
- SRE tabletop run and one live canary run with rollback drills.
